title: I'm a guy that doesn't like AI art. I'm vibecoding a game anyways.
author: Great_Necessary4741
selftext:
I'm the kind of person that doesn't personally like AI "art" where AI makes stuff for you without any human input besides prompting and paying for a subscription. So why am I vibecoding a game? Am I a massive fucking hypocrite?

Short answer: **yeah**. Long answer?

I use AI like I believe it should be most of the time: as a tool to help me with my life and personal projects. I don't usually tell ChatGPT "Hey AI please make this entire thing for me" I ask it questions to guide me through the process of doing something myself. However recently, I've really had this itch to play something like Call of Duty Zombies on my Steam Deck and I don't have the money to buy an actual Call of Duty game right now and I felt like I probably wouldn't have much fun playing an FPS on my Steam Deck anyways. But what I DO have at the moment is a ChatGPT Plus subscription that hasn't expired yet and Godot 4.7 installed on my computer. So I decided "fuck it, I'll get the AI to make me top-down COD Zombies" and that's how my slop game Dead Signal was born. 

Dead Signal is, like I said, a top-down clone of Call of Duty Zombies designed around controller play on the Steam Deck in both handheld mode and playing on the couch. Or in my case, my bed. It's got about everything the original game has: zombies, guns, perks, power-ups, that mystery box that plays a sound that weirdly traumatized me as a kid, etc. It was made almost entirely with ChatGPT as that's the AI I pay a subscription for, but I did use Claude for the shaders. Honestly been thinking of switching from ChatGPT because my god I fucking hate the ChatGPT CEO and don't want to give him any of my money but it's hard to switch when you've gotten used to something. Been working on it over the past few days, around 4-5.

The only human-made assets in this are the free sounds and music I got from resources like OpenGameArt and [Itch.io](http://Itch.io), though some that I couldn't find good ones for was made with ElevenLabs. There's also a unique song for the title screen made with Suno because as much as I don't like AI "art" damn it, it can make some catchy shit. That's kind of my whole problem, I'm in kind of a moral middle-ground with AI stuff rn and don't want to lean too far into either pro-AI or anti-AI because I'd alienate and ruin my reputation with a TON of people I know. Dead Signal to me is like a guilty pleasure kind of thing, I don't exactly LIKE that I'm making it but damn it it's a pretty fun game and I can't deny it.

I don't know if I'll ever release this publically in any capacity in the future because it's a strictly personal project at the moment and I don't really want myself tied to this. I plan on making a few more additions to make it a more fun experience and more like something you'd get for cheap on XBox Live Arcade in the 2010s. Achievements are a pretty high priority for me, also want to get split-screen multiplayer implemented at some point.

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body: Looks good. There shouldn't be a vision change for simply equipping a sniper rifle though. Maybe you run around using scope as your only vision irl but most people dont. You could change it so it narrows only when you're about to aim/fire.

replies.author: Great_Necessary4741
replies.body: The vision change only happens if you're scoped in, it narrows your view and zooms the camera out to simulate the view you'd get with an actual sniper scope. You have to be zoomed to get the most effective use out of the weapon because it can headshot the zombies to insta-kill them.

replies.author: Xinnobun
replies.body: Oh gotcha, nice. I guess I was thrown off when you were running around with the narrow vision. I see it now.

replies.author: Great_Necessary4741
replies.body: Yeah I should probably refine it's mechanics a little bit, like maybe add a slight slowdown or at least disable sprinting when scoped in.

replies.author: Xinnobun
replies.body: indeed, or even stop movement. Any of those choices help balance risk in using the sniper rifle.

replies.author: Great_Necessary4741
replies.body: I'll do a rebalance of it tommorow, I spent the rest of the day working on a level editor that lets me make my own blockouts that ChatGPT can decorate and add to the game, that way I have more control over map gimmicks and where to put them. Currently working on an abandoned trampoline park map that has working trampolines that let you bounce over zombies.
